transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (TideFluent Eng), Marta Silva (TideFluent PM), Evan Cho (TideFluent Security), Sana Idris (TideFluent DevOps)

Summary:
Quick handoff for the marketplace connector/adapter design. Focus on packaging (helm/chart), VPC and KMS compatibility, quantization/perf tradeoffs, canary routing and billing metering. Agreement to run a staging lab with sample model and verify telemetry.

Topics:
- Adapter API shape and expected gRPC vs HTTP proxying
- Packaging: helm chart + operator vs sidecar adapter
- KMS integration and HSM tenancy patterns
- Quantization recommendations and perf knobs
- Canary routing and billing meter hooks for marketplace listing

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, auto-transcript style, some mis-hears) ---
[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick, uh, agenda up front, we want to make sure TideFluent's adapter for Redwood marketplace is ops-ready and we hand off a runnable example. Priya is going to lead on perf/quant notes.
[00:20] Jordan Kim: Thanks Alex. We mostly want to understand the minimal integration surface — we don't want a huge rewrite of our runtime.
[00:27] Priya Shah: Totally. We're thinking the adapter exposes a small gRPC shim that maps the Redwood REST/chat calls internally to your model server. That avoids duplicating tokenization logic.
[00:40] Marta Silva: Quick Q — does that mean you expect us to do tokenization client-side or can Redwood supply a tokenizer container?
[00:47] Priya Shah: Good question. We support either. For faster latencies we recommend server-side tokenization in the adapter so the KV cache and prefix caching works correctly. But we can provide a tokenizer image if you'd rather keep the model immutable.
[01:05] Jordan Kim: If we do server-side tokenization, what's the memory footprint? Our model is 8-bit quantized and we have a tight GPU/host ram on edge nodes.
[01:15] Priya Shah: The tokenizer itself is small. The main memory is KV cache for long context lengths — depends on max_seq. We'll send you a sizing table.
[01:28] Alex Mercer: Also, packaging options — sidecar vs helm operator. Liam, can you summarize the tradeoffs?
[01:35] Liam Ortega: Sure. Sidecar is simplest for existing deployments; adapter runs next to model process, no cluster operator needed. Helm/operator gives easier lifecycle and marketplace upgrades, can manage canary rollouts and reconcile CRDs. For the marketplace listing we recommend providing both flavors: quickstart (sidecar) + production (helm operator).
[01:55] Jordan Kim: We prefer sidecar for initial pilot, operator for production — makes sense.
[02:02] Sana Idris: On network: we run private subnets with strict egress. We'll need clear outbound endpoints for Redwood control plane and for metrics ingest.
[02:12] Alex Mercer: Right — we have a VPC peering flow or private-link option. For on-prem we'll use a connector that establishes outbound TLS to Redwood's control plane. We'll share the whitelist IPs and hostnames after the call.
[02:28] Evan Cho: KMS question — do you require our keys to be in Redwood-managed KMS or can we keep them in our HSM? Our compliance team prefers customer-managed keys.
[02:38] Priya Shah: You can keep keys in your KMS/HSM. Our agent supports external KMS via KMS provider plugin (we've seen AWS KMS, Google CMEK, and Vault HSM integrations). We just need to exchange the key IDs and some IAM role set up. There is a small latency hit for envelope unwrap — usually sub-10ms, but we'll measure.
[02:58] Marta Silva: Great. On billing and usage metering — how do we expose per-inference metering to the marketplace so TideFluent can invoice usage?
[03:07] Alex Mercer: We emit fine-grained tokens and request metrics via the adapter. The adapter includes hooks to report token counts and inference durations to marketplace metering endpoints. We'll provide a sample meter forwarder (webhook or s3 sink) you can run.
[03:25] Jordan Kim: Are those hooks synchronous in the critical path? We can't add tail latency if metering blocks.
[03:31] Priya Shah: Metering is async by default — uses a local buffer and a batched send. You can plug in Kafka or push to our telemetry proxy.
[03:42] [Speaker 1 mislabeled] Jordan: ok that helps 
[03:47] Alex Mercer: Let's talk model variants and quantization. For TideFluent's model, you mentioned you'd like to offer both fp16 and an int8 quantized variant to hit price points?
[03:58] Jordan Kim: Yes, customers want lower-cost option. We're exploring 4-bit/8-bit quantization.
[04:05] Priya Shah: 4-bit can reduce memory but may impact quality. We have quantization guidance: per-layer calibration, use QLoRA-like flows for finetuned models but for base models we recommend GPTQ or AWQ for inference. We'll send a short doc with expected latency vs quality tradeoffs.
[04:24] Jordan: Please do — last time we saw big delta on long-form completions.
[04:30] Priya: Right, we recommend running small eval prompt set and measuring perplexity + task-specific metrics. Redwood Optimize can also run the evals if you want.
[04:42] Marta: Can Redwood host the evals or should we provide privada datsets? 
[04:48] Priya: Either. For PII/regulated content, run the eval internally and share metrics. If you can share synthetic prompt sets that's enough for us to iterate.
[04:57] Alex Mercer: On SSO, RBAC and audit logs: will TideFluent need organization-level SSO for the marketplace listing?
[05:06] Evan Cho: Yes, SSO and audit trails are mandatory, plus per-customer role separation. We need proof of SOC2 type II and role-based audit logs.
[05:15] Alex Mercer: Redwood has SOC2; we'll share our compliance pack and our log export formats. We also support SAML and OIDC for SSO.
[05:25] Jordan Kim: For the adapter, what logging level is required? We don't want workloads with verbose logs in prod.
[05:31] Priya Shah: Default is INFO. We expose structured logs and sampling for debug traces. You can turn on debug for canary windows only.
[05:42] Sana Idris: About canary routing — we want traffic splitting by tenant and percentage. Does the helm operator support traffic-level routing?
[05:52] Liam Ortega: Yes, the operator integrates with the Redwood routing mesh; you can declare a rollout CRD that maps percentage to the adapter version. We'll share a canary manifest example.
[06:05] Jordan Kim: Perfect. On the packaging: will you require a signed helm chart for marketplace?
[06:11] Alex Mercer: For the marketplace listing we require provenance: signed chart, SBOM, container image digest and vulnerability scan report. That's standard.
[06:20] Marta Silva: About SBOM — we use internal base images. Do you accept our SBOM or do you scan?
[06:26] Priya Shah: We accept your SBOM but will run an independent scan as part of listing gating. We'll share the scanner results.
[06:35] Jordan Kim: Are there any infra compatibility gotchas? We use Calico CNI and strict PSPs.
[06:41] Liam Ortega: We test against Calico and standard PSPs. We'll flag any RBAC needs and required capabilities (e.g., NET_ADMIN only if doing hostNetworking). But we generally avoid hostNetwork.
[06:54] Alex Mercer: Let's call out the live test plan: we'll run a staging lab that deploys the sidecar adapter to your cluster in our staging account, run 5-minute QPS bursts at three sizes, collect latency p50/p95 and token counts, confirm KMS unwrap latencies, and verify canary rollout and billing signals.
[07:12] Jordan Kim: Timeline?
[07:14] Alex Mercer: If we get the sample model by next Friday (12/10), we can schedule the lab for week of 12/13. That fits your Q4 runway?
[07:22] Marta Silva: Yes, that works for internal stakeholders. We'll share the model and a couple of perf targets.
[07:28] Evan Cho: For KMS we'll share a test key and an HSM integration contact. Note: production keys require extra paperwork.
[07:36] Priya Shah: Noted. We'll limit the test key to unwrap-only and remove it after the lab.
[07:43] [Minor crosstalk] Jordan: cool, thanks
[07:47] Alex Mercer: Any blockers on TideFluent side we should know about?
[07:51] Jordan Kim: Only that our packaging team is heads-down until 12/06. We'll free up someone after that.
[07:58] Sana Idris: Also, our cluster has egress proxies with TLS interception, could break cert pinning if the adapter is doing mutual TLS.
[08:08] Priya Shah: We can make TLS mutual optional and support mTLS through Envoy sidecar if needed. We'll put the options in the spec.
[08:18] Jordan Kim: One more — licensing. Do we need to sign a separate runtime distribution agreement for the adapter if we ship it as open-source?
[08:27] Alex Mercer: If TideFluent wants to open-source the adapter, that's fine; the marketplace listing still requires a commercial agreement for billing/marketplace fees. Legal can follow up.
[08:37] Marta Silva: Good.
[08:40] Alex Mercer: Ok let's recap next steps — (1) Redwood shares adapter API draft, helm chart example, canary manifest, and compliance pack; (2) TideFluent shares sample model tarball, mini-eval set, and KMS test key details; (3) run staging lab week of 12/13.
[08:59] Jordan Kim: Sounds good.
[09:02] Alex Mercer: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in an email with links to the repo and the docs.
[09:08] [Call ends, small wrap up chatter]
